Q: generate nuspec file for solution? A:

This is a very late coming answer, but I created a .nuspec file manually for my scenario that closely matches this question. I have a project of .NET assemblies, many with interdependencies, but can be considered on the whole as one large library. While developers can pull just the exact libraries they need, sometimes they just want to get started pulling all of them.

I created a .nuspec file that has all the same metadata as each individual package, added every package available in the whole library to the <dependencies> tag, and then didn't include a <files> tag. It works perfectly.

You can find it here: https://github.com/dahall/Vanara/blob/master/Vanara.Library.nuspec

Q: Are there programs concerning the notion of ineffable ordinal? A:

AI will almost always confirm whatever you ask it. This doesn't mean much. AIs are eager to please (so eager, they'll end up imagining non-existent things or confabulating so much it's tantamount to a lie, in order to give a pleasing answer). It's good to keep that in mind.

For example, everybody here is asking you to clarify. You are using an english word ('ineffable') and there is no High Dictator that is the one and only source of truth on the meaning of such english words. Anybody can come up with a concept, write a paper naming their concept 'ineffable', and now there are conflicting definitions. There is no trademark system for mathematical concepts. Nobody is going to sue you, nor will a magazine refuse to publish your paper, if it might engender confusion. AI is not magical - it has no better idea as to what you are talking about than any expert would.

Thus, if you ask AI 'does such an algorithm exist', it'll find any algorithm anywhere that anybody sort of kind of called 'ineffable' and respond with 'yeah, it exists!'.
